I will estimate the causal effect of years enrolled in a charter school on standardized 8th-grade math using instrumental variables (2SLS) that leverage the admissions randomization; for the main analysis I will restrict to applicants eligible for the city's second independent draw and use second_draw_offer as the instrument to reduce bias from the May confirmed-placement roster and its automatic after-school tutoring tied to initial offers. The first stage will regress charter-years on second_draw_offer plus lottery-cell fixed effects (school × grade × year) and baseline covariates (baseline_math, frl, parent_college, dist_charter, sibling_charter, n_ranked); the second stage will regress 8th-grade math on the predicted charter-years from that first stage. This identifies a local average treatment effect for second-draw compliers; I will report clustered robust SEs at the lottery-cell level, first-stage F-statistics, and weak-instrument-robust inference. The main threat is violation of the IV exclusion restriction and related channels: initial offers confer confirmed-roster status that automatically enrolls students in district after-school math tutoring (so lottery_offer may affect outcomes through services other than charter enrollment), and second-draw instruments may still be endogenous if entry into the second draw or take-up differs systematically or if the instrument is weak. I will therefore run sensitivity analyses including (a) IV using lottery_offer and comparing estimates, (b) reduced-form and intent-to-treat by lottery-cell, (c) bounds and weak-IV robust procedures, and (d) complier subgroup analyses to assess heterogeneity and residual bias.

lottery_offer | violated
second_draw_offer | plausible
dist_charter | doubtful
sibling_charter | doubtful
n_ranked | doubtful
INSTRUMENT: second_draw_offer

I will estimate the causal effect using an instrumental-variables (2SLS) design that exploits randomized initial lottery offers as an instrument for years enrolled in charter middle school, including lottery-cell fixed effects so identification comes from within-lottery random assignment. The treatment is years enrolled in charter school, the outcome is standardized 8th-grade state math score, the main instrument is lottery_offer, and I will include baseline_math, FRL, parent_college, n_ranked, sibling_charter, dist_charter and cohort/year fixed effects as pre-specified covariates to improve precision and check balance. I will report first-stage strength (F-stat), reduced-form effects, cluster standard errors at the lottery-cell (school-grade-year) level, and estimate LATE for compliers; as robustness I will use second_draw_offer in the eligible subsample and report IV overidentification and heterogeneity. The main threat is violation of the exclusion restriction — lottery_offer could affect test scores through channels other than charter attendance (placement roster effects, access to services, peer composition, or differential attrition/nonresponse), so I will run placebo outcomes, Lee bounds for attrition, and sensitivity analyses that control for post-lottery mediators. If the exclusion restriction looks questionable I will present reduced-form intent-to-treat estimates and bounds rather than a causal IV point estimate.

I will estimate the causal effect of years enrolled in a charter middle school on standardized 8th-grade math scores using a two-stage least squares (2SLS) IV design that exploits random assignment in the admissions lotteries: lottery_offer is the primary instrument (offers increase charter enrollment by ~0.9 years) and identifies the LATE for compliers. I will include lottery-cell fixed effects (school × grade × year) to absorb stratification and run the first stage of years_in_charter on lottery_offer (and second_draw_offer as a secondary instrument in overidentified checks where it is observed). The second stage regresses standardized 8th-grade math on the predicted years_in_charter from the first stage, controlling for pre-treatment covariates to improve precision (baseline_math, frl, parent_college, n_ranked, dist_charter, sibling_charter) and restricting to oversubscribed applicants as in the sample. I will report ITT estimates, first-stage F-statistics, cluster standard errors at the lottery-cell level, and interpret coefficients as the effect for lottery compliers under monotonicity and the exclusion restriction that offers affect outcomes only via enrollment. To probe the exclusion restriction I will test for balance on pre-treatment outcomes and run placebo outcomes, and I will run sensitivity analyses using second_draw_offer where available and report bounds if necessary. Key variables: outcome = standardized 8th-grade math score; treatment = years_in_charter; instrument = lottery_offer; fixed effects = lottery_cell; covariates = baseline_math, frl, parent_college, n_ranked, dist_charter, sibling_charter.

Key variables are outcome = standardized 8th‑grade state math score, treatment = years enrolled in a charter school, instrument = lottery_offer (and a sensitivity IV using second_draw_offer in the restricted subsample), with baseline_math and lottery‑cell fixed effects included to improve precision. The main threat is violation of the exclusion restriction or differential attrition — winning an offer could affect scores through channels other than enrollment (access to the confirmed placement roster/district programs, peer sorting, or administrative follow‑up differences), or the instrument could be weak in subgroups. I will report ITT and reduced‑form alongside IV, check first‑stage F‑statistics, test balance on pre‑treatment covariates, examine attrition patterns and baseline falsification tests, and only rely on IV if these diagnostics support the instrument. If diagnostics indicate exclusion or attrition problems I will present ITT/reduced‑form estimates as the more credible estimates and not use IV as the primary causal claim.

Estimate a local average treatment effect via two-stage least squares (fuzzy IV) of years enrolled in a charter on standardized 8th-grade math, restricting to the subsample that participated in the city's second independent random draw so the instrument is randomized. First stage: regress years_enrolled on second_draw_offer plus lottery-cell fixed effects and precision controls (baseline_math, frl, parent_college, sibling_charter, n_ranked, dist_charter); report first-stage F and balance tests. Second stage: regress 8th-grade standardized math on the predicted years_enrolled with the same controls and lottery-cell FEs, clustering SEs at the lottery-cell or applicant-cohort as appropriate. I justify second_draw_offer as the main instrument because it is randomized among non-winners, increases enrollment by about 0.6 years, and—unlike initial lottery offers—did not trigger the district’s universal after‑school tutoring program (so the exclusion restriction is more plausible); I will nevertheless test for direct effects on placebo outcomes and report IV, ITT (by offer), and OLS estimates. If second_draw_offer is too weak or sample-restricted, I will present ITT by lottery_offer (noting violation of exclusion due to the tutoring program) and run robustness checks using distance and ranking variables only as sensitivity analyses under stronger assumptions.

I will estimate a local average treatment effect (LATE) of years enrolled in a charter middle school on standardized 8th-grade state math scores using two-stage least squares, exploiting randomized admissions offers as instruments and including lottery-cell fixed effects to respect the randomization strata. Key variables are the endogenous treatment (years enrolled in a charter school), the outcome (standardized 8th-grade state math score), baseline_math and other pre-treatment covariates (frl, parent_college, dist_charter) for precision, and instruments lottery_offer and second_draw_offer; I will report first-stage F-statistics and balance tests. To address this, my primary IV will be second_draw_offer (valid for the subsample entered into the independent second draw and not exposed to the May tutoring), with sensitivity checks using lottery_offer (adjusting for any measured tutoring receipt) and bounding analyses for plausible violations. I will also test robustness to weak instruments, differential entry into the second draw, and attrition, and report intention-to-treat and complier-average effects.

The principal threat to identification is violation of the IV exclusion restriction: initial lottery winners were placed on the district’s confirmed placement roster (per the program memo) and thus may have received district after-school math tutoring regardless of actual enrollment, creating a direct channel from lottery_offer to test scores. To address that, I will attempt to control for confirmed-placement/tutoring receipt (if available), compare IV estimates with OLS and bounding approaches, and report sensitivity analyses excluding applicants on the confirmed roster. If confirmed-placement data are unavailable or manipulation is suspected, I will present estimates but emphasize the potential bias from this violated exclusion restriction.

Identification strategy: plan a two-stage least squares framework using lottery_offer as the canonical instrument for years enrolled in a charter (with lottery-cell fixed effects and rich baseline controls) because lotteries provide randomized variation and lottery_offer raises charter exposure by about 0.9 years. Key variables: treatment = years enrolled in a charter school; outcome = standardized 8th-grade state math score; controls = baseline_math, frl, parent_college, sibling_charter, n_ranked, dist_charter and lottery-cell fixed effects. Main threat: the exclusion restriction for lottery_offer is plausibly violated because the program memo states initial-offer holders were placed on the district's confirmed-placement roster and the district automatically enrolls rostered students in a free after-school math tutoring program, creating a direct channel from the instrument to test scores independent of charter enrollment. I also considered second_draw_offer (random among non-winners, +0.6 years) but it is missing for many applicants and identifies a selected subsample, and I considered distance-to-charter, sibling_charter and number-ranked as instruments but all are likely endogenous to unobserved neighborhood or parental factors. Because of the confirmed-roster→tutoring pathway I do not believe any instrument in these files satisfies the exclusion restriction for estimating the causal effect of years enrolled, so I will not use IV to estimate years-enrolled effects. Instead I will report ITT (offer vs non-offer) estimates with lottery-cell fixed effects and conduct sensitivity analyses and transparent bounds to show what would be required for a causal years-enrolled estimate.

Key variables are the outcome (8th-grade standardized math score), treatment (years enrolled in a charter), instrument (second_draw_offer), randomization strata fixed effects (lottery-cell: school–grade–year), and precision covariates including baseline_math, frl, parent_college, sibling_charter, dist_charter, and n_ranked. The main threat is a weak or imprecise first stage (and consequent finite-sample bias) or limited external validity because the IV identifies compliers only; additionally, initial lottery_offer is invalid for IV because it confers district tutoring independent of enrollment.
